program_name: Economics of Innovation for Sustainable Development (EISD). Italian official designation: 'Laurea magistrale in Economics of Innovation for Sustainable Development (Classe LM-56 R) [0404M21]'. French official designation: 'PARCOURS - Economics of Innovation for Sustainable Development', a parcours of a French 'diplome national de master controle par l'Etat' delivered by Universite Cote d'Azur (EUR ELMI), RNCP code 41077. Apply@UniTo course record id 704.
level: master (second-cycle degree / laurea magistrale / French Master 1 + Master 2; 2 years nominal duration, 120 ECTS). The programme opened in September 2024 and its first cohort was due to graduate in 2026.
teaching_language: Fully English-taught, and it falls into category (3) of the field definition: it is an INTERUNIVERSITY / INTERNATIONAL JOINT DEGREE, not a stand-alone UNITO degree and not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree. Apply@UniTo states 'Study language: English' and the UNITO microsite key-information sheet states 'Language: English'; the whole published curriculum (Innovation and Sustainable Development, Statistics and Econometrics, Economics of innovation in the energy sector, Finance strategy and new business models, Research design in economics, Academic presentation and writing, etc.) is listed in English. The degree is jointly awarded by the University of Turin (Department of Economics and Statistics 'Cognetti de Martiis') and Universite Cote d'Azur (Ecole Universitaire de Recherche ELMI, Nice); Universite Cote d'Azur describes it as 'un diplome conjoint multilingue reconnu par les gouvernements francais et italien' (a joint MULTILINGUAL diploma recognised by the French and Italian governments), and one of the three stated programme objectives is 'offrir aux etudiants des activites propices au developpement et au renforcement de leurs competences linguistiques' (to offer students activities conducive to developing and enhancing their language skills). [uncertain] The 'multilingual' label plus the generic ELMI master-application page statement 'Le niveau de langue demandee : C1 en Francais' raises the question of whether some French-language competence is expected in the Nice year; no EISD-specific page states a French requirement, and every EISD-specific admission text names only English C1.
campus: TWO campuses, split by year. The UNITO microsite key-information sheet states 'Location: Nice and Turin' with 'Reference Departments: Economics and Statistics Cognetti de Martiis and EUR ELMI'. Universite Cote d'Azur states 'La premiere annee du Master se deroule a l'Universite de Turin et la deuxieme annee a Universite Cote d'Azur' (Year 1 in Turin, Year 2 in Nice). Turin side: Department of Economics and Statistics 'Cognetti de Martiis', School of Law, Political and Economic-Social Sciences, University of Turin, Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino. Nice side: EUR ELMI, Campus Saint Jean d'Angely, 5 rue du 22eme BCA, 06300 Nice, tel. +33 4 89 15 20 01. Note that the Apply@UniTo record and the microsite footer box both reduce this to 'Study location: Italy, Turin' / 'Teaching seat: Turin', which reflects only the UNITO half.
degree_class: LM-56 (Scienze dell'economia / Economics). UNITO publishes it as class 'LM-56 R' - the R suffix marking a joint/international degree - with internal UNITO course code 0404M21 and CINECA catalogue id 33368 (codicione 0010107335700001). Apply@UniTo course id: 704. On the French side it is a state-controlled national master's degree with RNCP code 41077. 120 ECTS over 2 years (Master 1: 756 contact hours; Master 2: 680 contact hours).
admission_type: SELECTIVE / RESTRICTED, with a very small quota, and NOT administered through the normal UNITO Apply@UniTo route. Universite Cote d'Azur publishes 'Capacite d'accueil : 7' (7 places) and a two-stage procedure: 'Une premiere selection sur dossier (admissibilite) donnera lieu a un entretien avec les membres de l'equipe pedagogique' (a first selection on the application file leading to an interview with the teaching team). Because the administrative seat of the course is at Universite Cote d'Azur, both the preliminary evaluation and the actual enrolment are handled on the French national platforms: the Mon Master platform for the first year (M1) and the eCandidat platform for the second year (M2); non-EU applicants residing abroad use the French 'Etudes en France' (Campus France) procedure instead of Mon Master. The Apply@UniTo course record 704 exists but carries no application form, no deadline, no fee block and no quota block - it displays only 'Not available for applying at the moment' and redirects the reader to the programme's own 'How to apply' page. [uncertain] UNITO's own Italian catalogue simultaneously lists the degree among the 'corsi di laurea magistrale ad accesso libero' (open-access second-cycle degrees) and en.unito.it lists it under 'Postgraduate degrees with free admission'; this is an administrative classification on the Italian side (there is no Italian numerus clausus decree and no Italian entrance exam) and it conflicts in substance with the French 7-place capacity and the mandatory dossier-plus-interview selection. Treat the programme as selective in practice.
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027, first year (M1), French/EU citizens and equivalents: applications are filed on the French national Mon Master platform, whose 2026 campaign calendar was - candidature (dossier submission) window 17 February 2026 to 16 March 2026; main admission phase opening Wednesday 3 June 2026 (admission offers for work-study formations released 12 June 2026); complementary phase ('phase complementaire') 19 June to 19 July 2026, with new applications submitted 19-25 June, institutional review 26 June - 9 July and second-wave replies 10-19 July 2026; withdrawal-management phase (GDD) 20 July - 30 August 2026. The UNITO microsite gives no date of its own and states only 'Application deadline: Please check the Mon Master website'. Second-year (M2) entry runs on Universite Cote d'Azur's eCandidat platform on a separate calendar. [uncertain] The Mon Master dates are the NATIONAL campaign dates read from French government and French education-press sources; the programme-specific Mon Master record (monmaster.gouv.fr/formation/0062205P/1800592UKMXH/detail) is an Angular single-page application behind Cloudflare and could not be read directly, so a programme-specific deviation cannot be excluded. Also note that as of the research date (1 September 2026) the entire 2026/2027 Mon Master cycle has already closed.
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU citizens residing abroad do NOT use Mon Master. The EUR ELMI master-application page states: 'Si vous etes candidat non-ressortissant de l'Union europeenne - Les candidatures doivent etre deposees sur Etudes en France' (applications must be filed on the Etudes en France / Campus France platform). The Etudes en France campaign for the 2026/2027 intake opened on 1 October 2025; closing dates are set country by country by the local Campus France office, French institutions issue their decisions before 30 April 2026, and candidates must reply before 31 May 2026 (no reply counts as a refusal). [uncertain] No programme-specific non-EU deadline is published on any unito.it, univ-cotedazur.fr or elmi.univ-cotedazur.fr page; the dates above are the generic Etudes en France calendar and applicants must check their own country's Campus France page. Because the administrative seat is in France and enrolment is French, the usual Italian non-EU route (Apply@UniTo call + Universitaly pre-enrolment + Italian consulate visa) does NOT apply to this programme, and the Apply@UniTo record carries no non-EU quota.
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination. Selection is by file review followed by a compulsory INTERVIEW. Universite Cote d'Azur: 'Une premiere selection sur dossier (admissibilite) donnera lieu a un entretien avec les membres de l'equipe pedagogique. Cet entretien permet d'apprecier les qualites du candidat (savoir etre, expression orale, clarte et coherence du projet professionnel) ainsi que sa motivation.' On the Italian side, UNITO's catalogue entry describes a specially appointed commission that checks the curricular requirements and then admits candidates to the TAPP (Test di Accertamento della Preparazione Personale / Personal Preparation Assessment Test), described as a 15-minute Skype interview. In addition, English proficiency must be evidenced by a test or certificate: 'Connaissance de l'economie generale, des mathematiques, des techniques quantitatives, de l'anglais (niveau C1 du CECRL : test ou certificat a delivrer)'. [uncertain] The TAPP/Skype-interview wording was read from a search-engine rendering of www.unito.it, which is Cloudflare-blocked to direct fetch, and it is not clear whether the TAPP and the French 'entretien' are the same single interview or two separate steps.
academic_requirements: 1) PRIOR DEGREE - Universite Cote d'Azur: 'Le master conjoint EISD est ouvert aux titulaires : d'une licence en economie ou en gestion (obtenue par la formation initiale ou la validation des acquis) ; d'un autre diplome de niveau L3 apres avis de la Commission pedagogique.' i.e. a bachelor's degree (licence, L3 level) in Economics or Management, or another L3-level qualification accepted after review by the Pedagogical Commission. Apply@UniTo states the entry qualification as 'First cycle diploma (BA, Undergraduate diploma)'. 2) CURRICULAR CREDITS (Italian side) - UNITO's catalogue entry requires a bachelor's degree or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable under current regulations, plus 18 CFU in Economics and 6 CFU in Statistics. 3) PLACES - 'Capacite d'accueil : 7' (7 places). No separate non-EU sub-quota is published. 4) EXPECTATIONS AT ENTRY (published identically by UNITO and UCA) - demonstrate social skills and a professional attitude; be able to use oral expression effectively; show a high level of writing skills; possess analytical and synthesis abilities; exhibit critical thinking and justify arguments; have a high certified level in English; display intellectual curiosity to gather and organise relevant information; show sufficient basic knowledge and skills in business management; have an advanced level in quantitative techniques; master the fundamentals of innovation economics; demonstrate a strong interest in and sensitivity towards sustainable development issues. 5) SELECTION CRITERIA - 'Student selection is based on the following academic criteria: Knowledge of general economics, mathematics, quantitative techniques, and English (level C1 of the CEFR: test or certificate required); Consistency between the previous course of study and the Master; Consistency between the Master and the professional project' (the UNITO page adds 'Redoublement' / repeat-year status as a further listed criterion). 6) No GPA or minimum-grade threshold is published anywhere for this programme. [uncertain] The '18 CFU in economics and 6 CFU in statistics' figure comes from a search-engine rendering of the Cloudflare-blocked www.unito.it catalogue page and could not be confirmed against a directly-read page; the ratio also differs from the credit rules used by the sibling UNITO LM-56 programmes. It is also unclear how the Italian curricular-credit rule and the French 'licence en economie ou en gestion' rule interact for a candidate applying through Mon Master.
language_requirements: ENGLISH - C1 (CEFR) is the requirement published on every EISD-specific page. UNITO admission page: 'Knowledge of general economics, mathematics, quantitative techniques, and English (level C1 of the CEFR: test or certificate required)' and, among the entry expectations, 'Have a high certified level in English'. Universite Cote d'Azur: 'La maitrise de l'anglais (C1) est requise.' No list of accepted certificates, no minimum IELTS/TOEFL scores and no medium-of-instruction waiver are published for this programme. ITALIAN - no Italian language requirement is stated (the Turin year is taught in English); UNITO offers an optional 'Learning Italian' service. FRENCH - no French requirement is stated on any EISD-specific page. [uncertain] Two conflicts must be flagged: (a) the Apply@UniTo record 704 states a LOWER bar - 'Applicants must hold an international certification certifying at least a CEFR B2 level of English language proficiency' - while both the UNITO microsite and Universite Cote d'Azur require C1; assume C1 is binding, since the actual selection is run by the French side. (b) The generic EUR ELMI master-application page states 'Le niveau de langue demandee : C1 en Francais' (C1 in French) and 'Tous les documents doivent etre traduits en francais par un interprete assermente'; this appears to be boilerplate for ELMI's French-taught masters, but because EISD applications physically pass through that same ELMI/Mon Master channel it is not certain whether the French-language and sworn-translation rules are also applied to EISD candidates. Applicants should confirm with eur-elmi.scolarite@univ-cotedazur.fr.
required_documents: No itemised document checklist is published on any unito.it page for this programme. What is documented: (1) the application is entirely digital - 'Procedure de candidature dematerialisee' / 'Toutes les candidatures sont dematerialisees et s'effectuent en ligne, aucun format papier ne sera accepte' (no paper applications accepted); (2) a complete Mon Master application file (dossier) is required for M1 and an eCandidat file for M2, and the file is what the admissibility stage is judged on; (3) an English C1 test result or certificate must be produced ('test ou certificat a delivrer'); (4) the file must evidence a clear and coherent professional project, since the interview scores 'clarte et coherence du projet professionnel' and motivation; (5) EUR ELMI adds two general instructions for master applicants - 'Fortement conseille : attestation de comparabilite du FEI de votre dernier diplome' (a statement of comparability from France Education International / ENIC-NARIC France for the last diploma is strongly recommended) and 'Tous les documents doivent etre traduits en francais par un interprete assermente' (all documents must be translated into French by a sworn translator); (6) EUR ELMI warns that 'Toute erreur de procedure, de formations, ou de composantes, entrainera un rejet automatique de la demande par la Commission Pedagogique' (any procedural error causes automatic rejection). Non-EU applicants abroad additionally complete the Etudes en France dossier (identity documents, diplomas, transcripts, language evidence, CV, motivation) and the consular visa steps. No Italian application fee applies, because the applicant does not go through Apply@UniTo. [uncertain] The precise Mon Master document list for this specific formation could not be read (the Mon Master formation page is a Cloudflare-protected single-page app), and it is not confirmed whether the French sworn-translation rule is enforced for an English-taught joint programme.

uncertainty_notes:
ACCESS PROBLEMS AND METHOD (research date 2026-09-01). www.eisd.unito.it, www.unito.it, en.unito.it and www.didattica-est.unito.it all refused or 403'd direct fetches from this environment (network-level refusal for the microsites, Cloudflare 403 for www./en.unito.it; r.jina.ai was also served a Cloudflare challenge). Sources were therefore obtained as follows: (a) apply.unito.it course 704 was read DIRECTLY and in full with a desktop browser user-agent, in both en_GB and it_IT - it is the origin of the 'Study language: English', B2 wording and 'Not available for applying at the moment' statements, and it is confirmed to carry no deadline, fee, quota or territory block; (b) the four EISD microsite pages (home, key_information, admission_requirements, how_to_apply, tuition_fees_and_financial_aid) were read from Internet Archive raw snapshots, verified via the archive's 'rel=original' header to be genuine www.eisd.unito.it captures - snapshots dated 14 January 2025 (admission_requirements, how_to_apply, key_information) and 15 March 2025 (tuition fees), with the pages' own last-update stamps of 18/06/2024, 23/08/2024, 18/06/2024 and 14/01/2025 respectively; (c) univ-cotedazur.fr and elmi.univ-cotedazur.fr were read DIRECTLY and in full (the UCA parcours page carries an explicit 'Mise a jour le 11 septembre 2025', making it the freshest official source in this dossier); these two consortium sites are in scope because the unito.it microsite's own 'How to apply' page links to them for this joint degree; (d) www.unito.it catalogue content was reconstructed from search-engine renderings only.

SPECIFIC UNCERTAINTIES:
1) ENGLISH LEVEL CONFLICT - B2 vs C1. Apply@UniTo course 704 says 'at least a CEFR B2 level'; the UNITO microsite admission page and Universite Cote d'Azur both say C1 ('test or certificate required'). Since the selection is actually run by the French teaching team, C1 should be treated as binding; the B2 line is most likely inherited boilerplate from other UNITO records. No accepted-certificate list and no minimum IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge scores are published for this programme at all, and no medium-of-instruction waiver is mentioned.
2) FRENCH-LANGUAGE AMBIGUITY. Universite Cote d'Azur calls the diploma 'multilingue' and lists language-skill development as a programme objective; the generic ELMI master-application page demands 'C1 en Francais' and sworn French translations of all documents. No EISD-specific page states any French requirement. It is unresolved whether an English-only applicant passing through the ELMI/Mon Master channel is subject to those generic French rules.
3) OPEN-ACCESS vs SELECTIVE CONFLICT. UNITO classifies the degree among its open-access ('accesso libero' / 'free admission') second-cycle courses, while the French side publishes a 7-place capacity and a mandatory dossier-plus-interview selection. Both statements are official. The practical reading is that there is no Italian numerus clausus decree or Italian entrance exam, but entry is nonetheless competitive and capped at 7.
4) DEADLINES ARE NOT PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC. The UNITO microsite deliberately publishes no date ('Please check the Mon Master website'). The 17 February - 16 March 2026 candidature window, the 3 June 2026 main admission phase and the 19 June - 19 July 2026 complementary phase are the NATIONAL Mon Master 2026 campaign dates; the programme's own Mon Master record could not be opened (Angular SPA behind Cloudflare; the public API returned 401). Some of the complementary-phase detail came from French education-press renderings rather than a directly-read government page. Note also that the whole 2026/2027 cycle had already closed by the research date.
5) NON-EU ROUTE IS FRENCH, NOT ITALIAN. Non-EU applicants residing abroad go through Etudes en France / Campus France, whose deadlines are set country by country; the generic 2026/2027 markers (campaign opens 1 October 2025, institutional decisions before 30 April 2026, candidate reply before 31 May 2026) are not programme-specific and were not read from a unito.it or univ-cotedazur.fr page. Conversely, the Italian Universitaly pre-enrolment / Italian consulate visa route that applies to other UNITO masters does NOT apply here.
6) CURRICULAR CREDITS UNVERIFIED. The '18 CFU in economics and 6 CFU in statistics' rule and the 'TAPP - 15-minute Skype interview' description both come from a search-engine rendering of the Cloudflare-blocked www.unito.it catalogue page. They could not be confirmed against a directly-read page, they do not appear on the eisd.unito.it microsite or on any French page, and it is unclear how they are applied to a candidate who files through Mon Master.
7) MICROSITE STALENESS AND TEMPLATE ERRORS. The archived EISD microsite pages date from 2024-2025 and the CampusNet template contains leftover absolute links to an unrelated UNITO microsite (www.digitalhumanities.unito.it), showing the site was cloned and not fully cleaned; the admission page also mis-names the programme once as 'the Master in Economic and Social Development (EISD)'. No 2026-dated capture of the microsite's admission or how-to-apply pages exists in the Internet Archive, so 2026/2027-specific changes on the UNITO side cannot be excluded.

9) FEES. The EUR 1,200 per year figure comes from a page last updated 14/01/2025 and is not tied to a stated academic year; the amount is fixed by the bilateral cooperation agreement and is paid to Universite Cote d'Azur, so neither UNITO's ISEE brackets nor the EUR 60 Apply@UniTo application fee apply. The CVEC (French student-life contribution, roughly EUR 100+ per year, amount not published on these pages) is due in the second year only. A current 2026/2027 figure could not be verified.
10) REQUIRED DOCUMENTS ARE NOT PUBLISHED. Neither UNITO nor UCA publishes an itemised checklist for this programme; the list given above is assembled from the digital-application rules, the English test/certificate requirement, the interview's stated scoring criteria and ELMI's generic master-application notice.
11) DO NOT CONFUSE with the other UNITO LM-56 English-taught masters: 'Economics' (2304M23, Apply id 282), 'Economic Analysis and Policy' (Apply id 683, EPOG-JM Erasmus Mundus), 'Economics of the Environment, Culture and Territory' (Apply id 291) and 'Economics and Finance with Data Science' (Apply id 705).
